# `set_wifi_country`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set the Wi-Fi regulatory country of the device.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xcdd70, ns_net::set_wifi_country @0x6fc4c0 (64-bit build) |

Runs the network script's country command with the supplied text, which is formatted unquoted into a shell command line, so whitespace splits it and shell metacharacters are interpreted (INFERRED). No format check is made; validation is left to the wireless driver, and the helper does not examine the command's exit status or output, so success does not show the country was applied or that the value was valid. A value equal to the stored code does nothing; otherwise the script applies the change in the background after the reply and restarts the access point. An empty string resets the country to the factory default. Clients MUST send only an uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

Side effects: Runs a shell command (no timeout) that stores the country and, in the background, stops the station supplicant and access point, applies the regulatory country and restarts the access point, briefly interrupting it.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_wifi_country"`. [READ] |
| `params` | string\|array\|object | yes | - | Wi-Fi regulatory country code. Three spellings: a bare string, a one-element array holding a string, or an object with country. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | params missing, null, an empty array, missing country key, or not a string | `expected string param` |
| 214 | The network script process could not be started | `fail to run command` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

No country-value validation error exists; the device never checks the value.

## Example

Request, object-form - Set country:

```json
{"id":61,"method":"set_wifi_country","params":{"country":"XX"}}
```

Request, scalar-form - Bare string:

```json
{"id":62,"method":"set_wifi_country","params":"XX"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_wifi_country","result":0,"code":0,"id":61}
```

Reply, missing:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_wifi_country","error":"expected string param","code":105,"id":63}
```
